thread:
josh (customer): Hey team — after I upgraded the @redwood/sdk to v0.20.0 my TS code started returning a 404 on responses.create. It used to work on v0.19.x. No other infra changes on our side. Anyone seen this?

liz (support): thanks for the report — can you paste the SDK call and the error payload + your SDK version? Also any request ids from logs?

josh (customer): sure. using node 18.16, @redwood/sdk@0.20.0. minimal repro:```ts
import { Redwood } from '@redwood/sdk'
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY })
await client.responses.create({ model: 'redwood-2.1', input: 'hello' })
```error:HTTP 404 { message: "route responses.create not found" }
no request id in body, but headers: x-rw-trace: trace-2026-9ab3
I also tried retries, still 404.

liz (support): odd. can you try the REST endpoint directly (curl) to see if the API exists?

josh (customer): curl works:```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/responses.generate -d '{"model":"redwood-2.1","input":"hello"}'
# returns 200 with text output
```so the REST route is responses.generate not responses.create. The SDK is calling responses.create and getting 404. Also when I tried to call responses.generate via the SDK I get a 400 validation error: missing parameter 'model_id' (??) even though I sent 'model'.

liz (support): that is super helpful. tagging eng. @anna can you take a look?

anna (ts-sdk): thanks, looking. quick theory: there was a rename in the SDK client surface in 0.20.0 where we standardized method names to .create and renamed the model param from model -> model_id (nullable->required change). If the backend version for the hosted API still expects responses.generate and field name model -> model, that would explain the 404 + 400 mix.

raj (eng-runtime): +1 on the mismatch theory. we rolled a minor router change to prefer new RPC names in the latest canary but didn't flip the hosted API routing for all regions. hitting it with the new SDK would 404. the validation error when you call the old endpoint via the SDK is because the SDK now serializes payloads with model_id and the server validation expects model.

anna (ts-sdk): immediate workarounds: 1) pin @redwood/sdk to 0.19.4 (npm i @redwood/sdk@0.19.4) — this will keep using responses.generate + old field names. 2) use the REST endpoint directly for the new behavior (call responses.generate) until we patch. 3) as a temporary dev workaround, call the SDK low-level .request method with manually shaped body:```ts
await client.request('POST','/v1/responses.generate', { body: { model: 'redwood-2.1', input: 'hello' } })
```should bypass the auto-rename.

josh (customer): pinning to 0.19.4 fixed it for now, thanks. Any ETA on a patch?

raj (eng-runtime): creating INC-2026 and assigning to eng-runtime + sdk team. We'll push a compatibility shim on the routing layer to accept responses.create -> responses.generate for hosted API and add server-side translation of model_id -> model. Hoping to ship a prod patch within 4 hours.

support-bot: INC-2026 created by liz (support) — assigned to eng-runtime, priority P2.

anna (ts-sdk): followup: we also missed a changelog note explaining the non-backwards-safe rename. We'll cut a 0.20.1 patch that preserves old method names as aliases and restores serialized field names to 'model' by default while we coordinate backend cutover. Expected publish in ~2h.

raj (eng-runtime): patch deployed to legacy routing in region-us-west and region-eu. should be live.

josh (customer): confirmed — upgraded back to 0.20.0 and calls now succeed. headers show x-rw-trace: trace-2026-9ab3 -> 200. Thanks for the fast turnaround :tada:

liz (support): great to hear. we'll keep INC-2026 open to track the proper SDK/server migration docs and changelog. Please ping if you see anything else.

anna (ts-sdk): published 0.20.1 to npm with compatibility aliases. recommend teams upgrade to 0.20.1 (fixes the rename regressions).

josh (customer): upgraded to 0.20.1 — working. appreciate the quick help.

liz (support): closing loop — leaving INC-2026 open until docs updated. thanks everyone.
